title: MCP server implemented from scratch, dependency-free (stdlib only)
evidence: server.py:84 MCPServer implements JSON-RPC 2.0 stdio, initialize handshake (server.py:133), tools/list, tools/call, resources/list+read; no MCP SDK imported
suggestion: None — a hand-rolled protocol layer with schema validation (server.py:50 validate) is a strength for a portable benchmark.

title: players(club='Flamengo') returns 0 rows against the real FIFA snapshot
evidence: _agent_stdout.log item_22: 'players Flamengo 0'; soccer.py:407 players() club filter is correct but the FIFA dataset (fifa_data.csv, a global snapshot) contains no Flamengo-club players
suggestion: Data limitation, not a code defect — nationality/club filtering itself works (test_soccer.py:218 test_player_filters_and_sorting passes club='Santos FC'). Worth documenting that Brazilian-club coverage in the FIFA file is sparse.

title: Cross-source deduplication with score-conflict retention and adjacent-day merge
evidence: soccer.py:170-201 merges the same match across the 5 overlapping feeds, keeps first-source score, and records conflicts (coverage() reports score_conflicts=9 on real data, _agent_stdout.log item_22)
suggestion: None — this goes well beyond the spec's 'load all 6 CSVs' and is verified by test_soccer.py:76 and test_2019_standings_do_not_double_count_sources (test_soccer.py:185).

title: Standings refuse to assert official champions/relegation from incomplete data
evidence: soccer.py:415 standings() sets complete_double_round_robin flag (False for 2023: 377/380 matches, _agent_stdout.log item_22) and returns dataset_leader with a caveat note rather than 'champion'
suggestion: None — honest handling of incomplete seasons; R9 (standings computed from matches) is satisfied and tested (test_soccer.py:185).

title: analysis() calls _page([], limit, 0) purely to validate limit
evidence: soccer.py:457 discards the result of self._page([], limit, 0) — an inline validation side-effect that is easy to misread as dead code
suggestion: Extract the limit-range check into a small helper (e.g. _check_limit(limit)) and call it directly for clarity.

title: Test suite exercises all 27 sample queries against the real datasets end-to-end
evidence: test_soccer.py:194 test_all_27_natural_language_examples_have_executable_tool_answers drives each SAMPLE_QUERIES entry through the MCP server; real-data row counts asserted (test_soccer.py:173); test_coverage=0.95, defect_rate=1.0 in scores.json
suggestion: None — R12 is well covered; 24 test methods (many parametrized via subTest), 0 skipped.
